Install over USB

This page installs drawbridge onto a phone plugged into this computer. Nothing is uploaded anywhere: the app is served from this site and goes straight down the cable.

Needs Chrome, Edge or another Chromium browser. Firefox and Safari have no WebUSB.

This browser cannot talk to USB devices. Open this page in Chrome or Edge, or use tools/provision-adb.sh from a terminal instead.

On the phone, first

  1. 1
    Remove every account. Settings → Passwords, passkeys & accounts. You sign back in at the end. Nothing else is erased.
  2. 2
    Delete the Private Space, if there is one. Settings → Security & privacy → Private Space. Android will not hand over the phone while a second profile exists, and this one is hidden from the user switcher. Deleting it removes what is inside it.
  3. 3
    Enable Developer Options: Settings → About phone, tap Build number seven times.
  4. 4
    Settings → System → Developer options → turn on USB debugging.
  5. 5
    Plug the phone into this computer.

Then, here

  1. Connect to the phone
  2. Check the phone is ready
  3. Download and verify drawbridge
  4. Install it
  5. Make drawbridge the owner


      

        
Now lock it again

        
    

  1. 1
    Open drawbridge. You can check the new version under ⋮ → Diagnostics.
    2. 

  2. 2
    Tap Lock drawbridge, and write down the key it shows. Locking mints a fresh one, so the key you had before stops working.
    3. 


        
Locking switches USB debugging off. It comes back when you unlock drawbridge with your key, which is how you would install a later version over the same cable.

      


      

        

          Installing drawbridge uninstalls the apps it blocks.
          
It starts within minutes of this install, not later on the phone. Move what you want to keep off it first — bookmarks, anything saved only inside an app. What a setting can still bring back waits until you lock.

        

        
Now finish on the phone

        
    

  1. 1
    Sign back in with a Google (or other) account, if you want one.
    2. 

  2. 2
    Set a screen lock.
    3. 

  3. 3
    Open drawbridge, choose the language, read the policy, set the options.
    4. 

  4. 4
    Tap Lock drawbridge and write the key down before leaving that screen.
    5. 


        
Locking switches USB debugging off. It comes back when you unlock drawbridge with your key, which is how you would install a later version over the same cable.

      


      
Updating a phone that already has drawbridge

      
Same page, same button. It notices the phone is already managed and updates it instead. Nothing is reset and nothing on the phone is lost. Try the phone first, though: drawbridge offers its own update on screen while it is still locked, and that route does not cost you your key. This cable is the fallback for when that will not go through.

      
    

  1. 1
    On the phone, open drawbridge and enter your key to unlock it. That is what hands USB debugging back.
    2. 

  2. 2
    Turn USB debugging back on: Settings → System → Developer options.
    3. 

  3. 3
    Plug the phone in and press the button below.
    4. 

  4. 4
    When it finishes, lock drawbridge again on the phone and write down the new key. Locking makes a fresh one, so your old key stops working.
    5. 



      
This page runs a small ADB client in your browser. It pauses Android's check on cable installs for the length of the copy, then puts it back exactly as it found it: on success, on failure, and if you unplug the phone.
